source.title: Deep Dreams Are Made of This: Visualizing Monosemantic Features in Diffusion Models

record.tranche_reason: Applies feature visualization and SAE disentanglement to latent diffusion models and reports how feature interpretations vary across diffusion time steps.
record.gate_note: The paper qualitatively compares raw layer channels with SAE features in Stable Diffusion and reports differences across activity peaks. It does not test language models, superposition or capacity pressure, nor whether the cited InceptionV1 neuron has a shared pose feature. Regularizer and noise-injection sweeps are discussed as visualization-quality calibration, not as measurements of polysemantic-neuron prevalence.
record.test_reason: This is a method paper. It assumes raw channels are polysemantic and uses an existing SAE to disentangle them. It reports only qualitative visualization quality for its own LVO method, raw-layer versus SAE variant, in one Stable Diffusion 1.5 layer. It does not measure the prevalence of polysemantic neurons, their cause, or how measurement choices change whether a neuron counts as polysemantic. The time-step results concern visualization quality, not polysemanticity classification.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that LVO extends feature visualization to latent diffusion models. SAE features give clearer, more consistent visualizations matching dataset examples than the raw-layer baseline. Regularizers transfer but need different settings for raw and SAE variants. LVO complements dataset examples and steering. The polysemanticity of raw channels is asserted from qualitative variety, not measured.
record.recipe_differences: Adapts feature visualization with gradient ascent to diffusion-model latent space; uses SAE features alongside a raw-channel baseline, activity-peak selection, schedule-matched noise, steering-based prior initialization, and latent-specific regularization.
record.method_sensitivity: Qualitative interpretations varied across time-step peaks for some features. Visualization results also varied with regularization and schedule-matched noise; the paper reports that SAE and raw-layer variants preferred different regularizers.

fits_no_version.finding: In SD1.5 up1.1, raw-channel visualizations (features 25 and 1214) were less coherent than SAE-feature visualizations, and their dataset examples were more varied. The authors call this consistent with polysemantic raw channels. Evaluation is qualitative, on the first 30 channels or features.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion-model U-Net layers, SAE features yield more coherent feature visualizations than raw channels.

fits_no_version.finding: Visualization quality for a feature varies across diffusion time-step activity peaks. The highest activation did not always occur on the most active peak (feature 10331).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Feature visualizations in diffusion models depend on the denoising time step chosen.

record.problems: Evaluation is qualitative, with no accepted or quantitative interpretability metric or statistical uncertainty. Empirical scope is one fine-tuned model, one layer, and the first 30 raw channels and SAE features; SAE training was reused from prior work.
record.rows_left_out: Calibration sweeps in Appendix G compare optimization and regularization settings, but are not recorded as separate rows because they assess visualization quality rather than the prevalence or semantic mixture of neurons, or explanation-scoring alternatives.

untested.parts: No image classifier is studied. The diffusion-model raw channels are labelled polysemantic only qualitatively, and the examples shown are related (animal parts).
No test of initialization, regularization or noise as causes.
No comparison of polysemantic share across architectures, activation functions or training choices, and no performance cost reported.
Canonical polysemantic neurons are not revisited.
No varying of activation-range cutoffs or explanation-scoring methods to see how polysemanticity classification changes. The time-step peaks affect visualization quality only.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V7 'tested' status and its labels are not supported. The time-step peak differences concern optimization success, not whether neurons count as polysemantic. Zoom In is cited as background only. All evidence is qualitative, from a single model and layer.

versions.untested_parts: The study uses a diffusion image generator, not an image classifier, and does not demonstrate raw neurons responding to several unrelated semantic input kinds. Its raw-channel examples are animal-related parts/species or butterfly-like visualizations and noise.
No language models, transformer MLP neurons, or token/context responses are studied.
No capacity-pressure or feature-count mechanism is tested.
No initialization, regularization, or training-noise cause of polysemanticity is tested.

The study compares raw and SAE representations and tunes visualization regularizers, but does not measure the share of polysemantic neurons across architectures or activations, or task performance costs.
The study does not revisit canonical polysemantic neurons or establish that their unrelated inputs share a feature such as pose. Its SAE feature visualizations are not a test of the cited neuron.
It tests qualitative visualization differences across diffusion time-step peaks, but not alternative explanation-scoring methods or activation-range cutoffs within a time step.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 1.5 (Style50), raw layer feature 25
rows.stage_stated: fine tuned on the UnlearnCanvas Style50 dataset
rows.operation_detail: Optimized feature visualization and inspected dataset examples for the raw channel
rows.value: Visualizations mixed fur and animal-part textures; examples were dogs, cats, and bears, with no single species. The paper describes eyes, noses, paws, feathers, and fur across peaks.
rows.note: The reported examples vary within animal-related content, so they do not establish unrelated semantic input kinds.
rows.check: This is a diffusion U-Net, not a classifier. The examples are all animal-related, so they do not show unrelated inputs. The authors' polysemantic label is an assumption, not a measured result.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 1.5 (Style50), raw layer feature 1214
rows.stage_stated: fine tuned on the UnlearnCanvas Style50 dataset
rows.operation_detail: Optimized feature visualization at each reported activity peak
rows.note: The paper reports a different outcome at the later peaks.
rows.check: Butterfly-like visualization at one time-step peak shows the method working at that peak. It does not show the neuron's polysemantic status depending on activation range or scoring, so it does not bear on V7.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 1.5 (Style50), raw layer feature 1214
rows.stage_stated: fine tuned on the UnlearnCanvas Style50 dataset
rows.operation_detail: Optimized feature visualization at each reported activity peak
rows.note: Contrasts with the butterfly-like result at time step 1.
rows.check: Noise at later peaks is a visualization failure (adversarial maxima). It is not a measure of polysemanticity under a different activation range.

rows.subject: Stable Diffusion 1.5 (Style50), SAE feature 9984
rows.stage_stated: fine tuned on the UnlearnCanvas Style50 dataset
rows.operation_detail: Optimized feature visualization at activity peaks
rows.measure: Qualitative interpretation across activity peaks and seeds
rows.value: Colorful strokes oriented top-left to bottom-right appeared consistently across peaks; dataset examples shared the diagonal composition.
rows.note: This is a case where changing the time-step peak did not change the reported interpretation.
rows.check: An SAE feature's consistency across peaks is the study's own method output. It is not a test of V7, and 'absent' is not meaningful here.

rows.check: Visualization of an SAE feature measures the study's method performance, not the polysemanticity of neurons.
